Explanation

Your application has hardcoded URLs that might correspond to services that are not accessible on Azure.

Review and ensure that the application is attempting to access URLs that would be available from Azure. You might need to migrate those services to Azure too, this way you will get the benefit of lower latency in the cloud.

If your application needs to depend on services that run on-premises, you can connect your Azure and local networks with ExpressRoute, Hybrid Connections, or VPN solutions.
Local or network IO operations detected
 Potential 3
FilePosition
src\eShopWinForms\Views\CatalogView.csLine 57
src\eShopWinForms\Views\CatalogView.csLine 57

Explanation

Your application has local or network IO operations.

If you are targeting Managed Instance on Azure App Service, move persistent I/O to storage mounts (Azure Files/UNC). Keep local writes to temp only; connect to external dependencies via private endpoints/VNet to reduce latency.

IO operations outside of the application folder might not be available on Azure App Service. Review and ensure IO APIs are attempting to access paths that will be available when your app is running on App Service sandbox. If you choose the containerized hosting option, your scenario still might be broken or have scalability issues.

Possible solutions:
1. Files that the application needs can be deployed with the application or put in Azure Storage. You can use Azure Storage File Shares as a drop-in replacement for on-premises file share.
2. Other services that the application depends on might need to be migrated to Azure, this way you will get the benefit of lower latency in the cloud.
3. If your application needs to depend on services that run on-premise, you can connect your Azure and local networks with ExpressRoute, Hybrid Connections, or VPN solutions.
Local OS environment access detected
 Potential 1
FilePosition
src\eShopWinForms\Views\CatalogView.csLine 56
src\eShopWinForms\Views\CatalogView.csLine 56

Explanation

Local OS environment access detected.

If you are targeting Managed Instance on Azure App Service, Read config via App Settings or App Configuration; avoid machine‑specific environment APIs. Persist environment setup via install scripts when needed.

When running in Azure App Service environment, your application can read environment variables that you define in App Service settings. Using environment API other than reading environment variables might indicate that your application depends on some local machine's features and might be broken on App Service sandbox or not scale well. Review your scenarios and either refactor them to be more cloud friendly or choose the option in App Service to host your application in the sandbox for Windows Container Web Apps.

If you choose to use other Azure hosting options such as Azure Container Apps (ACA) or Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS), environment APIs might work, however scaling still might be an issue.
SQL database connection detected
 Potential 3
FilePosition
src\eShopWCFService\Web.config

Explanation

SQL database connection detected.

Ensure the database is available/reachable on Azure.

If it is not, there are multiple ways you can move your data to Azure:
1. Migrate to Azure SQL Database.
2. Consider Azure SQL Managed Instance if you need features that are not available in Azure SQL Database and you don’t want to use a VM.
3. Migrate your database servers directly to SQL Server on Azure VMs.

To assess database migration effort, you can use Azure Migrate tool, see the link below.
Connection strings without configuration builders detected
 Optional 3
FilePosition
src\eShopWCFService\Web.config
src\eShopWCFService\Web.config

Explanation

Connection strings without configuration builders detected.

Keeping connection strings directly in the app is not the best practice and might introduce security risks, increased maintenance, scalability challenges or compliance standards (such as PCI DSS, GDPR, etc.).

Instead, it is recommended to use configuration builders to get secrets from secure sources in Azure environment.

src\eShopWinForms\eShopWinForms.fx.csproj

Explanation

Static content detected.

Your current approach of serving static content directly might lead to increased costs, performance issues, maintenance challenges (requiring application redeployment for content changes), and security risks.

Consider moving static content to Azure Blob Storage and adding Azure CDN.
Upgrade to newer target framework to get better cloud experience
 Optional 3
FilePosition
src\eShopWCFService\eShopWCFService.csproj

Explanation

Upgrade to newer target framework to get better cloud experience.

If you are targeting Managed Instance on Azure App Service, validate on .NET Framework 4.8 or move to .NET 10. Persist any runtime prerequisites via install scripts; test in staging before production.

While if targeting other Azure compute services:

Application targeting .NET framework lower than 4.7.1 might missing features that would be needed for some cloud scenarios like scaling or getting secrets from secure external sources.

Azure App Service runs apps on .NET Framework 4.8 or .NET Framework 3.5. Apps running on on .NET Framework versions older than .NET Framework 4.8 could have potential compatibility issues. It is recommended to test your application running on .NET Framework 4.8. Note that it is not necessary to re-target to .NET Framework 4.8, only to validate that the app correctly runs on that version of .NET Framework.

In the long term it is also recommended to upgrade your application to latest supported .NET 8+ which would significantly increase performance of your application. Use tools like .NET Upgrade Assistant to help with upgrading your application to newer .NET.
System.Data.SqlClient dependency detected
 Optional 3
FilePosition
src\eShopWCFService\Web.config

Explanation

System.Data.SqlClient dependency is detected.

While System.Data.SqlClient will work in Azure, the newer Microsoft.Data.SqlClient package is the primary .NET SQL client moving forward and receiving the latest features. For example, Microsoft.Data.SqlClient easily allows use of Azure Managed Identity from a connection string.

Explanation

API is binary incompatible for selected .NET version: affects existing binaries, often requiring recompilation, because the API has changed in a way that prevents older binaries from loading or executing.
Project's target framework(s) needs to be changed
 Mandatory 1
FilePosition
src\eShopWCFService\eShopWCFService.csproj
src\eShopWinForms\eShopWinForms.csproj

Explanation

Project's target framework(s) needs to be changed to the new target framework that you selected for this upgrade.

During upgrade target framework will be adjusted to corresponding platform when applicable. In some cases project would result in multiple target frameworks after the upgrade if it was using features that now have their own platforms in modern .NET frameworks (windows, iOS, Android etc).
Project file needs to be converted to SDK-style
 Mandatory 1
FilePosition
src\eShopWCFService\eShopWCFService.csproj

Explanation

Project file needs to be converted to SDK-style. Modern .NET framework projects require a change in the project file format and use SDK corresponding to project flavor and functionality.
WCF Client APIs
 Mandatory 1
FilePosition

Explanation

WCF client-side APIs for building service clients that communicate with WCF services. These APIs are available as exact equivalents via NuGet packages - add System.ServiceModel.* NuGet packages (System.ServiceModel.Http, System.ServiceModel.Primitives, System.ServiceModel.NetTcp, etc.)
Legacy Configuration System
 Mandatory 2
FilePosition

Explanation

Legacy XML-based configuration system (app.config/web.config) that has been replaced by a more flexible configuration model in .NET Core. The old system was rigid and XML-based. Migrate to Microsoft.Extensions.Configuration with JSON/environment variables; use System.Configuration.ConfigurationManager NuGet package as interim bridge if needed.
GDI+ / System.Drawing
 Mandatory 1
FilePosition

Explanation

System.Drawing APIs for 2D graphics, imaging, and printing that are available via NuGet package System.Drawing.Common. Note: Not recommended for server scenarios due to Windows dependencies; consider cross-platform alternatives like SkiaSharp or ImageSharp for new code.
Windows Forms Legacy Controls
 Mandatory 3
FilePosition

Static assessment of only D:\a\eShopModernizing\eShopModernizing\eShopModernizedNTier. The solution connects a desktop catalog client to one WCF service; diagrams describe implemented calls and separately label deployment declarations, not verified running infrastructure. [A1–A6]

Data Storage & External Services

The service owns one context containing five entity sets; SQL Server is the configured provider and LocalDB is the named fallback. Compose declares a separate SQL Server container, not another application service. There is no cache, broker or external API call in the traced service/client path; their existence outside this scope is unknown. [A3, A5–A10]

Key Architectural Decisions

  • View events drive a presentation controller; startup manually supplies the generated proxy and view. There is no active container-based DI in this path; the alternative registration module is commented out. [A2, A3, A16]
  • Service operations directly use EntityModel rather than a separate repository layer. Catalog display composes item and discount responses in the desktop controller. [A3, A5]
  • Build/runtime settings diverge: desktop target is .NET 6, legacy desktop project and App.config refer to Framework 4.7.1, service targets Framework 4.6.1, and its container tag is 4.7.2. These are declarations, not a verified compatibility result. [A8, A9, A11, A17, A18]

API & Service Communication Contracts

Scoped source defines ten SOAP operations at one WCF address, not ten REST URLs. The desktop uses synchronous request/reply calls, although the generated proxy also offers Task-based variants of the same operations. [S1, S2, S3]

Service Catalog

ServicePortCategoryPurpose
eShopWCFService / eshopwcfserviceCompose host 5113 → container 80; development IIS URL uses 5200BusinessCatalog, discounts and dated availability; WCF with EF 6.1.3. Ports are deployment/development declarations, not live observations. [S4, S5, S6]
eShopWinFormsNo listener declaredAPI consumer / desktop presentationGenerated System.ServiceModel 4.8.0 client; no gateway role. [S3, S7]
sql.dataCompose host 5433 → 1433Infrastructure, third-party containerSQL Server deployment dependency, not a source-built API. [S4, S8]

Solution membership identifies two application projects and Docker orchestration, not a fleet of microservices. [S9]

API Endpoints Inventory

All rows below use POST /CatalogService.svc with a SOAP envelope and operation-specific action. This method/protocol interpretation follows the BasicHttpBinding declaration and generated SOAP actions, not REST annotations. The action prefix is http://tempuri.org/ICatalogService/; suffixes are the operation names below and replies append Response. No explicit API versioning or typed FaultContract is declared. Communication Patterns

  • Synchronous: UI controller calls generated WCF methods on the startup/UI path; server uses direct DbContext calls. Generated Async methods are client alternatives, not queue/event messaging. No broker, gateway, service discovery or client load-balancing configuration is present in the traced path. [S2, S3, S10]
  • Composition: desktop separately requests catalog items and today's discount, then combines them for display. A failed call is not replaced with cached or empty data: this path has no catch/retry/circuit breaker/fallback. [S3]
  • Resilience: no explicit operation/open/send/receive timeout values are set in the generated binding or supplied App.config binding; effective framework defaults are unverified. Buffer/receive-size limits are int.MaxValue (2147483647); reader quotas are Max; cookies are allowed. No application retry policy is configured. [S14, S15]
  • Address resolution: Program's parameterless generated client selects a code-defined HTTP localhost:5113 address. App.config contains an equivalent address, but changing it alone does not alter this generated constructor path. [S7, S14, S15]
  • Startup dependency: client loads data before opening its dialog; server requires database connectivity when queried. Compose declares SQL startup ordering without a health-conditioned dependency. Full deployment details are in D:\a\eShopModernizing\eShopModernizing\eShopModernizedNTier\.github\modernize\assessment\engines\facts\configuration-inventory.md. [S7, S8, S10]
  • Security posture: inspected operation implementation has no identity, role or resource-ownership checks. The active client address and explicit service endpoint use Basic HTTP without configured credentials/transport-security customization. HTTPS protocol mapping and HTTPS metadata are declared, but no concrete TLS listener/certificate is established by these files. Actual IIS/network access restrictions remain unknown; public Internet accessibility is not established. Exception details in SOAP faults are disabled. [S5, S10, S14, S15]

Core Business Workflows

Users browse and filter a product catalog, see date-based sale prices, query stock availability and record stock for an arrival date. These are the workflows traced in the scoped desktop/service sources; no ordering, payment or shipment-fulfillment lifecycle is established. [B1–B4]

EntityService / Bounded ContextDescriptionKey Relationships
CatalogItemCatalogService / catalog managementProduct offered for browsingClassified by brand and type; referenced by dated inventory. [B5, B6]
CatalogBrandCatalogService / catalog classificationProduct brand lookupUsed by products and UI filters. [B5, B1]
CatalogTypeCatalogService / catalog classificationProduct category lookupUsed by products and UI filters. [B5, B1]
CatalogItemsStockCatalogService / dated inventoryAvailable quantity for one product/day; UI calls this a shipmentLogical association to product, not a full shipment aggregate. [B2, B3, B6]
DiscountItemCatalogService / promotionsGlobal date-bounded discount used for catalog displayNo product-specific association; client applies selected discount to displayed items. [B1, B2, B5]

These are descriptive business groupings, not independently deployed bounded contexts or explicit DDD aggregates. Persistence fields/mappings belong to D:\a\eShopModernizing\eShopModernizing\eShopModernizedNTier\.github\modernize\assessment\engines\facts\data-architecture.md.

Primary Workflows

Workflow 1: Browse catalog with current promotion

  1. Startup manually constructs client/controller/view and calls LoadView before showing the window. LoadView checks the promotion banner, loads items, loads brand/type filters, then populates inventory-selection lists. [B1, B4]
  2. Filter changes emit an event; controller clears the grid and requests matching products using the All-filter rule. [B1, B3]
  3. Service returns products, then controller independently requests today's discount using Active-promotion selection. No matching discount means normal prices, not an outage fallback. [B1, B2]
  4. View applies Displayed-price calculation, loads each local image and renders the catalog. A separate initial discount lookup builds the sale-end banner. [B1, B3]

The grid is cleared before the remote requests complete. No application-level recovery restores it if communication/image loading fails. Re-evaluation uses client local time, not an authoritative server-supplied business calendar. [B1, B3]

Workflow 2: Record or replace dated stock availability

  1. User chooses a product, quantity and arrival date; the form applies Availability-entry parsing. [B3]
  2. Controller constructs a stock request and sends it to the service. [B1]
  3. Service finds a same-product/calendar-day record and applies Stock replacement, otherwise New-record identity allocation. [B2]
  4. After the remote call returns, the form displays success and clears entry controls. Failure has no compensating action or business fallback in this path. [B1, B3]

Despite the UI's shipment wording, adding availability replaces an existing day's number; it does not increment a running stock balance or track delivery status. [B2]

Workflow 3: Check stock for a selected day

  1. User selects a product from the inventory list and a calendar day. The form extracts the product ID from display text and emits a search event. [B3]
  2. Controller requests availability. Service chooses the first matching product/day row and applies Missing-stock result. [B1, B2]
  3. View appends a result row; it does not replace previously displayed results. No cumulative-through-date calculation is performed. [B2, B3]

Workflow 4: Initialize sample business state

The context registers a create-if-missing initializer. On seed execution it inserts types, brands, products, stock and discounts through separate save calls. Sample promotions and stock use 2017 dates; current-day sale activity cannot be assumed from seed data. [B7, B9] This is initialization, not a scheduled replenishment or promotion job.

Other contract operations provide item create/update/delete/find and lookup retrieval; the traced desktop exposes browsing and stock controls, not a complete catalog maintenance workflow. [B1, B2, B10]

Cross-Service Data Flows

Only desktop-to-business-service communication is established. The desktop joins catalog and promotion responses in memory for display; brand/type responses build filter choices, and product IDs connect inventory selection to availability requests. There is no cross-microservice aggregation, event choreography, saga, broker or circuit-breaker fallback in this chain. [B1, B2, B4]

The normal absence cases are null promotion → no discount, missing product → null and missing dated stock → zero. These are business-data decisions, not substitute responses for an unavailable downstream service. Exceptions are not caught in these controller/service methods, so outage behavior is not a graceful degradation contract. [B1, B2]

Business Workflow Sequence

sequenceDiagram participant User participant Form as "CatalogView" participant Controller as "CatalogController" participant Service as "CatalogService" participant Stock as "Dated inventory in EntityModel" User->>Form: Record quantity for product and arrival day Form->>Form: Check required selections and parse input alt Required selection or text missing Form-->>User: Return without recording availability else Input passes presence checks and parses Form->>Controller: Submit availability event Controller->>Service: Send stock record Service->>Stock: Look up same product and calendar day Stock-->>Service: Existing record or none alt Existing record Service->>Stock: Replace quantity and save else New day for product Service->>Stock: Allocate identifier and insert then save end Service-->>Controller: Completion Controller->>Form: Notify successful recording Form-->>User: Show success and clear entry fields end Note over Form,Service: Parsing transport and persistence failures have no business fallback here

Sequence evidence: [B1–B3]. An invalid nonempty quantity/date can throw during parsing; it does not follow the silent missing-input branch.

Business Rules & Decision Logic

RuleImplemented decisionEvidence
All-filter ruleZero disables the corresponding brand/type filter; nonzero values must match. Both active filters are combined with AND.[B1, B2]
Active-promotion selectionInclusive start/end calendar dates; first match after materialization, no explicit ordering or overlap priority.[B2]
Displayed-price calculationConvert decimal price to double, multiply by 1 - discount.Size, format with F and prepend a dollar symbol; banner rounds size × 100 to zero decimals. No persisted discounted price is written.[B1, B3]
Availability-entry parsingMissing product selection, empty quantity or empty date returns silently; otherwise uses int.Parse and Convert.ToDateTime. No positive-quantity check or TryParse recovery is implemented here.[B3]
Availability-search parsingAssumes a selected item and parses the ID prefix from display text; no null-selection guard in this handler.[B3]
Stock replacementFirst record for same product/date is assigned submitted quantity rather than increased. Date comparisons ignore time.[B2]
New-record identity allocationItem and new stock keys use maximum existing key plus one. No empty-set handling or concurrent allocation protection is implemented in these service methods.[B2]
Missing-stock resultNo matching record yields zero; no running total across earlier dates.[B2]
Declared model validationBrand/type strings each have StringLength(50); service operation methods add no explicit validation routine, discount range check or uniqueness check. Enforcement beyond these declarations is not tested.[B2, B5]

State transitions: records are inserted, overwritten/updated or removed; no order/shipment/promotion lifecycle state machine is modeled in the inspected entities and service. [B2, B5, B6]

Transactions and integrity: each mutation explicitly saves; there is no enclosing multi-call transaction, saga or compensation. Stock references a product by identifier without service-level existence validation. Unidirectional item brand/type references do not have reciprocal collection-maintenance logic. [B2, B5–B7]

Errors, audit and authorization: the inspected controller/service path has no business exception translation, retry, audit trail or identity/role/ownership checks. This describes source behavior only; deployed database/IIS policies and external audit systems are unknown. [B1, B2, B11]

Gaps: workflows were not executed; culture-sensitive parsing/formatting, concurrent writers, actual seed execution and host-side errors remain unverified. The mock is not a proven fallback: live Program constructs the remote client, DI registrations are commented, and mock discount lookup throws NotImplementedException. [B4, B12, B13]

Compatibility, supported-lifecycle status and CVEs were not verified by this build-file-only assessment; no advisory scan, restore or build was run. [D1–D4]

Data Ownership Boundaries

One service context holds all catalog, lookup, stock and promotion records. The desktop accesses them through service contracts; it combines catalog and discount responses for display, not by querying another service's tables. No database-per-business-service separation, CQRS read model, outbox or event-driven replication is implemented in the inspected paths. [P1, P6, P7, P14] The LocalDB fallback and environment-selected SQL server are alternative connection choices, not demonstrated replicas or two simultaneously used stores. [P3, P4]
